passage: I'm Jaya, and last year my father, Gautam, changed the rules almost overnight. I'd started at a new school, gone quiet at home and stopped saying where I was going. He began texting every hour, then decided I couldn't go out after school at all. At first I only felt watched. Later I realised he looked shut out, standing by the door when I came in. So I tried something. Before he could ask, I'd say, "Going to the library with Anu, back by six." Then a photo of the shelf. It felt silly at first. After some weeks he stopped texting. One evening he said, "You don't have to tell me everything, but thank you." I felt lighter, and so, I think, did he.

qa.q: What did Gautam do when Jaya stopped saying where Jaya was going?
qa.a: He began texting every hour and then decided Jaya couldn't go out after school.

qa.q: How did Jaya's father seem to feel, judging by the way he stood at the door?
qa.a: He looked shut out and worried, waiting for Jaya to tell him what was happening in her life.

qa.q: What did Jaya do that changed things, and why did it help?
qa.a: Jaya shared plans before he asked, which lowered his need to check and let Jaya earn more freedom.

qa.q: How might Gautam have felt when Jaya told him about the plans?
qa.a: Probably relieved and reassured, because it answered his worry and made him feel included again.

grounding: Shows a teen whose parent clamps down out of worry and who shares plans freely to reduce the need to control.

passage:
I'm Eshaan. The year I turned fifteen, I changed fast. New friends, like Sahil from the skating group, earphones in all the time, one-word answers at dinner. And Mom clamped down. Suddenly there was a curfew, questions about every message, and my door had to stay open.
I thought she was being a jailer. Then one night I heard her on the phone with Masi: "He's become a stranger in my own house. I feel shut out." Her voice cracked.
That hit me. I had been shutting her out and calling her controlling for noticing.
So I tried something. Every morning I told her my plan for the day: where, with whom, when back. I brought Sahil home to meet her. It felt silly at first. But within a month the open-door rule vanished, and the curfew moved an hour later. Sharing freely got me more freedom than fighting ever did.

qa.q: Who was Eshaan's new friend from the skating group?
How did Mom feel when Eshaan changed?
qa.a: Shut out and hurt; she said he had become a stranger in her own house, and her voice cracked.

qa.q: What did Eshaan do that lowered Mom's need to control?
qa.a: He told her his plans each day, where, with whom and when back, and brought Sahil home to meet her.

qa.q: How did Eshaan's view of Mom change after the phone call?
qa.a: He stopped seeing her as a jailer and saw a worried mother who felt shut out.

grounding: A teenager whose mother clamps down after he changes learns she feels shut out, and by sharing plans freely lowers her need to control and gains freedom.

passage:
Counsellor's note, family session
Mrs. Kalyani Iyer asked for this meeting. Since Uma stopped dance class and began spending evenings in her room, her mother has been taking her phone at nine, checking her bag and banning sleepovers. "I don't know my daughter any more," she said, and then, quietly, "I feel locked outside her life."
Uma rolled her eyes, then saw her mother's face and stopped. She said she quit dance because she was tired of it, not because of anything bad, and that her evenings were mostly music and one friend.
I suggested a small experiment: Uma tells her mother her plans for each weekend and introduces the friend; her mother drops the bag checks for a month. Both agreed. At the follow-up, Mrs. Iyer said, "She tells me things now. I don't need to search."

qa.q: What did Uma say she mostly does in the evenings?
qa.a: Music, and time with one friend.

qa.q: How did Mrs. Iyer feel about Uma's changes?
qa.a: Worried and shut out; she said she felt locked outside her daughter's life.

qa.q: What experiment did the counsellor suggest?
qa.a: Uma shares her weekend plans and introduces her friend, and her mother drops the bag checks for a month.

qa.q: What changed for Uma when she saw her mother's face?
qa.a: She stopped rolling her eyes, seeing that her mother was hurt rather than simply controlling.

grounding: A counsellor's note shows a parent who clamped down after her teen changed and feels shut out, and how the teen's open sharing reduces the need for control.
